title: What Is Remittance? Meaning, Inward and Outward Remittance, and LRS
summary: What is remittance? Learn the remittance meaning in English and Hindi, how inward and outward remittance work in India, and the LRS limits and TCS rates.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


Have you ever paid a foreign supplier, received payment from a client in the U.S. or transferred tuition funds to an overseas university? Each amount paid is considered a **remittance** . The volumes involved can be enormous. In 2025–26, Indian workers overseas sent a record[$110.47 billion back to India](https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-economics/remittances-india-finances-fy26-no-long-term-fix-10733712/) . There are certain rules and limitations for remittance, both inward and outward, so let’s start with the basics.


### Key Takeaways


- Remittance refers to funds transferred between people or businesses, typically across international borders. Inward remittances are received in India. Outward remittances are sent out of India.
- Resident individuals can remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme for permitted purposes. Corporates, partnership firms, HUFs and trusts cannot use this scheme.
- From 1 April 2026, TCS is payable at a rate of 2% on the portion of remittances for education and medical treatment above ₹10 lakh, and on overseas tour packages from the very first rupee. A rate of 20% is charged for other LRS purposes above ₹10 lakh. The threshold is annual; qualifying education-loan remittances are exempt.
- Inward remittances need the appropriate purpose code. You may receive documentation from your bank or provider, such as a FIRC or remittance advice, depending on the transaction.


##


What Is Remittance? Meaning and Examples


A remittance is when money is sent from an individual or business to another. Typically, remittances are made abroad. The sender makes a remittance and the recipient receives the money into their bank account. The term can also describe domestic transfers, but this guide focuses on cross-border remittances involving India.


The Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999 covers foreign-exchange remittances made from India to overseas countries. They are channeled through Authorised Dealers, including AD banks authorised by RBI to handle foreign exchange transactions. The permitted route depends on the sender, purpose and transaction type.


For example, money sent by a person working abroad to their family in India is an inward remittance from India’s perspective.


##


Types of Remittance: Inward and Outward Remittance


Remittance is classified by direction, and as a result there are two types of remittance. There are various documents, limits and taxes to consider depending on the remittance going into the country or out of the country.


### Inward Remittance Meaning


Remittance which is sent from abroad to India is known as **inward remittance** . It may be when you receive payment from an overseas client, receive funds from an NRI or a foreign investor invests in your business. Foreign investment has separate reporting requirements; it is not treated as an ordinary export receipt.


Inward remittances received for export of goods or software are reported by the bank receiving the funds through the Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS), as applicable. EDPMS is linked to the RBI; it is not the reporting system for every personal transfer or investment receipt.


Remittances have a[purpose code](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/purpose-code-for-international-payments/) to show why they have been sent. Choose the code that matches the actual service or goods supplied, rather than applying one software-export code to every transaction.


An e-FIRC (electronic Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate) may also be given by your bank. The[FIRC or remittance advice](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/firc/) can be used as proof of receipt for relevant export records. Depending on the payment route, the document may instead be called FIRS or FIRA. Exporters may also need an eBRC and applicable export-reporting records. Confirm the required document with your bank for your payment route.


### Outward Remittance Meaning


An[outward remittance](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/outward-remittance-meaning/) is any money that goes out of India, such as paying a university in Canada, paying for a vacation in Dubai, buying permitted shares on the NASDAQ or sending money to a relative overseas.


Travel is a common purpose for outward remittance. Studies overseas, maintenance of relatives and permitted investments are other examples. Business payments, such as paying a foreign supplier, also qualify as outward remittances but do not automatically fall under an individual’s LRS allowance.


**Basis** **Inward remittance** **Outward remittance**


Direction Into India from abroad Out of India to another country


Common examples Export payments, NRI transfers, foreign investment Tuition fee, travel, overseas investment, financial assistance to relatives


Important documents or details Purpose code, remittance advice or e-FIRC where applicable; export or investment records as required PAN, Form A2 declaration and purpose-specific supporting documents

##


Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) Explained


Permitted outward remittance by resident individuals can be carried out under the **Liberalised Remittance Scheme** . It was launched by the RBI on 4 February 2004, with a limit of USD 25,000. Here’s how the scheme works under the[RBI’s LRS directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?Id=10192) :


- **Accessibility:** All resident individuals are allowed to use it, even minors. The declaration form is countersigned by a minor’s natural guardian.
- **How much:** Up to USD 250,000 per financial year (April to March) across all permitted transactions, current and capital, combined.
- **How often:** As many times as desired, not exceeding the annual limit. After hitting it, you can’t make further remittances under the standard allowance that year, even if the investment proceeds are returned to India.
- **Documents:** PAN is required and all transfer purposes are provided in Form A2. The bank may also request invoices, admission letters or other supporting records.
- **Who cannot use it:** Corporates, partnership firms, HUFs or trusts are not eligible to use it. LRS is for FEMA-resident individuals, not every Indian passport holder living abroad.
- **What is not allowed:** Remittances for margins or margin calls to overseas exchanges, foreign-exchange trading abroad, lottery tickets and other prohibited transactions. Restrictions also apply to capital-account remittances to FATF-designated non-cooperative countries and territories, and transfers to specified high-risk entities.


Certain education, medical treatment and emigration remittances can exceed the standard limit under specified conditions and supporting estimates. Check the applicable exception with your AD bank before arranging the transfer. Company remittances follow their applicable FEMA rules rather than LRS.


### TCS on Outward Remittance: Rates from 1 April 2026


The Tax Collected at Source (TCS) is collected by banks and other authorised dealers on applicable LRS transactions exceeding certain amounts. In Budget 2026, the education and medical treatment rate was reduced from 5% to 2%. The new rates apply from 1 April 2026 and are contained in Section 394 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, as amended by the Finance Act, 2026.


[ICICI Bank’s remittance guidance](https://www.icici.bank.in/nri-banking/nriedge/nri-articles/looking-to-send-money-abroad-know-about-outward-remittances) sets out the standard rates and exemptions below:


**Purpose** **Up to ₹10 lakh** **Amount above the ₹10 lakh annual threshold**


Education funded by a qualifying loan from a specified financial institution Nil Nil


Education funded from other sources Nil 2% on the excess amount


Medical treatment abroad Nil 2% on the excess amount


Overseas tour programme package 2% from the first rupee 2% on the package amount; no ₹10 lakh exemption


Any other LRS purpose Nil 20% on the excess amount


Note: The ₹10 lakh LRS threshold is assessed on the aggregate remittances for the year, not separately for each transfer or bank. Overseas tour packages follow a separate collection rule, generally through the package seller. TCS can be claimed as a tax credit while filing an income tax return; it is not automatically an additional final tax cost.


For example, if your only LRS remittance during the year is ₹12 lakh for education funded from savings, standard TCS is 2% of ₹2 lakh, or ₹4,000. Bank fees, exchange-rate costs and applicable service taxes are separate.

##


Get Your Cross-Border Payments Right from Day One


Remittance flows support families, education, travel and business. Before collecting or sending money, check its direction, purpose and the applicable route:


- Process inward remittance from overseas payers with the appropriate purpose code and retain the applicable e-FIRC or remittance advice.
- Before any outward remittance under LRS, monitor the USD 250,000 limit, as well as the 2026 TCS rates and exemptions.
- Display TCS and FX on the bill before payment is made by the customers, alongside any other applicable charges.

##


FAQs About Remittance


#### 1. What is remittance in simple words?


Funds transferred between individuals or entities, typically from one country to another, like paying a supplier abroad.


#### 2. What is remittance meaning in Hindi?


Remittance का हिंदी अर्थ “धन प्रेषण” है। इसका मतलब किसी व्यक्ति या व्यवसाय को पैसे भेजना है, आम तौर पर एक देश से दूसरे देश में।


#### 3. What is the difference between inward remittance and outward remittance?


Inward remittance is money received in India from abroad, such as an export payment. Outward remittance is the money that is remitted out of India to another country, for example, tuition fees paid to an overseas university.


#### 4. What is the difference between payment and remittance?


A payment settles a purchase, bill, or invoice, whether the other party is in India or abroad. A remittance is money sent to another person or business, usually across borders. It can be a payment, such as settling an overseas supplier’s invoice, or a personal transfer, such as a gift or money for a relative living abroad.


#### 5. How much can I send abroad under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme?


Up to USD 250,000 per financial year (April to March) for permitted purposes, split across as many transfers as you want, subject to the scheme’s conditions and specific exceptions.


#### 6. Can a company send money abroad under LRS?


No. The scheme is only for resident individuals, including minors. Corporates, partnership firms, HUFs, and trusts cannot use it.


#### 7. Is TCS charged on outward remittance?


Yes, above set thresholds for applicable transactions. From 1 April 2026, rates of 2% apply to education not funded by a qualifying loan and medical transfers above ₹10 lakh, and tour packages from the first rupee. Other purposes attract 20% above ₹10 lakh, and qualifying loan-funded education attracts none. The LRS rates apply to the excess over the annual threshold.
